reflections.title: "Blessed with Every Spiritual Blessing"

reflect.text: Many people think heaven is just an improved version of earthly fun. But the spiritual blessings Paul describes are an active reality right now. Through Jesus and His resurrection, we are already linked to the heavenly realm. Living with the risen Savior provides everything we need to walk wisely and follow God each day. We do not have to wait until the next life to receive His grace, God's undeserved kindness; His power helps us in the present.

Everything Jesus won by His life, death, and return to heaven belongs to those who trust Him. In love, He brought us into God's family as adopted children. Now, as our King and priest, He carries our names before the Father and speaks for us. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "His high estate is as much at our service as was his condition of abasement." We can face each day knowing all His wealth and care are ours.

questions: How does knowing you are already joined to Christ change the way you face your daily routine?
In what ways can you lean on Christ's constant care and prayers for you today?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for giving us every blessing in the heavenly realms right now. We are grateful that You hold us in Your care, speak for us in heaven, and supply all we need to follow You. Help us to live each day in the strength of Your resurrection. Amen.

reflections.title: "Obtained an Inheritance"

reflect.text: God does not leave anything to blind chance. When we look at creation, every joint and muscle shows His careful design. In His daily care for the world, not even a sparrow falls without Him knowing it. Salvation is planned with that same perfect wisdom. God knows the end from the beginning, shaping each believer like a chosen stone placed into a grand, lasting building.

In this great plan, we have received a rich inheritance, but not because of anything good in ourselves. Our right to heaven belongs entirely to Jesus. As Charles Spurgeon noted, believers remain safe because "you are preserved in Christ Jesus." Because we belong to Him, all the rewards of His obedience are shared with us, giving us a secure future that can never be measured or lost.

questions: How does knowing that God has a wise plan for your life bring you peace during uncertain times?
Why is it comforting to remember that your place in heaven depends on Christ rather than your own efforts?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, we praise You for Your wise and unshakable purpose in saving us. Thank You that our eternal inheritance does not rest on our weak deeds, but on Jesus and His finished work. Keep our hearts steady in the assurance that You are holding us fast. Amen.

reflections.title: God’s Glorious Plan of Grace

reflect.text: God began His rescue plan long before time began. Adrian Rogers reminded believers that salvation is entirely God's work, meaning we cannot boast or bear the burden of keeping ourselves saved. Left to ourselves, we never would have sought Him, but He chose us in love. Because of Jesus, God does not look at us with anger; we are welcomed and delighted in as His beloved children. Our standing with Him does not rise and fall with our feelings, because Christ never changes.

Through the shed blood of Jesus, our sins are completely forgiven. Our deep debt is wiped away fully, freely, and forever, freeing us from fear and filling us with thankful worship. God has also placed His Holy Spirit within us as a deposit, guaranteeing the full inheritance to come. What we experience of God's goodness now is only a small foretaste of heaven, where every sorrow will end and we will share in Christ's everlasting joy.

questions: When your feelings make you doubt God's love, how does remembering your acceptance in Christ help you?
How does the gift of the Holy Spirit give you hope for the eternal life ahead?
reflections.prayer: Gracious God, thank You for choosing us, forgiving all our sins through Jesus, and accepting us in Your love. Thank You for the gift of Your Spirit, who assures us of the wonderful future You have prepared. Teach us to rest in Your grace and live with hearts full of praise. Amen.
